name: Directional smear (motion-blur approximation)
visual_intent: A word or object arrives (or leaves) too fast to see sharply: it is stretched along the motion and blurred in that direction only, then snaps crisp at rest.

performance_characteristics.memory_profile: Low; the SVG Gaussian blur is rasterised only while the target moves (filter detached at rest). Cost scales with target area (estimate, not measured on the M2).

implementation_summary: Per target: an SVG feGaussianBlur with stdDeviation 'x 0' (or '0 y') applied through CSS filter, tweened from strong to zero with the same ease as the move, plus a stretch along the motion anchored at the leading edge. The filter is attached for the move only (filter none at rest). Not true motion blur: there is no temporal supersampling.
runtime_api: Studio.fx.smear(tl, target, at, {side, distance, blur, stretch, duration, ease, stagger, exit})

validation.evidence: Runtime self-test (blur active and stretched mid-move, filter detached and transform reset at rest, hidden before entrance) in Playwright Chromium on Windows, 2026-10-30. SVG filter cost in HyperFrames on the M2 is not yet measured, so not approved.
